clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old man presented with a large right humeral lesion causing pathological fracture, associated with a nasopharyngeal mass and bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Imaging confirmed an aggressive lytic lesion of the right humerus. A Tru-Cut biopsy of the humeral lesion established the diagnosis of malignant metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Although the nasopharyngeal biopsy histopathology report confirming undifferentiated type III NPC is not directly documented, the clinical context and pathology from the metastatic site strongly support this diagnosis.
